name: Russia–Ukraine War
status: Active — Frontline fighting; trilateral talks set for Abu Dhabi
context: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched in February 2022, remains the largest conventional war in Europe since WWII. Fighting is concentrated in Donetsk Oblast, where Russian forces are slowly pushing into Kostiantynivka, and along the Hulyaipole and western Zaporizhzhia axes. ISW assesses that Russian gains in autumn 2026 have been marginal and that Moscow's claims of capturing 6,500 sq km in 2026 are inflated; Ukraine says October 2026 brought Russia's highest monthly losses of the war. Both sides continue daily long-range drone and missile strikes. After a local ceasefire in Oleshky in late October, the US, Russia and Ukraine agreed to resume trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11, though deep gaps remain over territory, NATO and security guarantees.

events.title: Abu Dhabi talks confirmed for Nov 10–11
events.desc: US envoy Steve Witkoff said US, Russian and Ukrainian delegations will resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week. Analysts expect no quick breakthrough given gaps over a ceasefire and security guarantees.

events.title: Zelensky confirms trilateral talks
events.desc: President Zelensky confirmed technical-level trilateral meetings with Russia and the US in the first half of November, backing a ceasefire that freezes current front lines.

events.title: Local ceasefire agreed in Oleshky
events.desc: Russia and Ukraine agreed a limited ceasefire in the embattled frontline city of Oleshky in Kherson Oblast, alongside plans for new talks.

events.title: Russian push into Kostiantynivka
events.desc: DeepState reported Russian forces gaining a foothold in north-western Kostiantynivka. ISW notes Russian and Ukrainian positions in the city are interspersed and disputes Moscow's broader claims.

events.title: Ukraine reports record Russian losses
events.desc: Ukraine's foreign minister said October 2026 saw Russia's heaviest monthly losses of the war, including a record 2,500 troops in a single day. Figures are Ukrainian claims.

name: Israel–Gaza War
status: Fragile ceasefire — phase two stalled, near-daily Israeli strikes
context: The war that began with Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack has been under a US-brokered ceasefire since October 2025, but the truce is fragile. Phase two of the Trump peace plan was declared in January 2026 after the last hostage remains were returned, yet the Palestinian Authority says it exists 'only on paper'. Israeli forces still control just over half of the Strip, Hamas has not disarmed, and Israel conducts near-daily strikes it says target militants. Gaza's Health Ministry reports more than 74,000 killed since 2023, including about 1,600 since the ceasefire. Israel's cabinet approved the entry of an International Stabilization Force in July 2026, with a pilot planned in Rafah under the Board of Peace, while hunger and displacement remain severe.

events.title: Ceasefire death toll nears 1,600
events.desc: Gaza's Health Ministry said Israeli attacks since the ceasefire took effect have killed 1,599 Palestinians and wounded 5,774. The overall war toll exceeds 74,000.

events.title: Near-daily strikes continue
events.desc: Israel keeps striking targets it describes as Hamas threats near the dividing line, while both sides accuse each other of violating the truce.

events.title: Hamas presses for Israeli withdrawal
events.desc: A Hamas delegation visiting Iran called for pressure on Israel to implement the ceasefire agreement and withdraw from the Strip.

events.title: Stabilization force preparations begin
events.desc: Israeli media reported preparations for deploying the International Stabilization Force in parts of Gaza, starting with a pilot in Rafah.

events.title: Israel approves stabilization force
events.desc: Israel's security cabinet approved the entry of an international stabilisation force operating in coordination with the IDF.

name: Myanmar Civil War
context: Myanmar has been at war since the military ousted Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government in February 2021. After disputed elections, Min Aung Hlaing handed command of the armed forces to Ye Win Oo in March 2026, and the military has regained some ground in the centre of the country. ACLED recorded more than 450 civilians killed in mass-killing incidents in the first half of 2026 alone. In Rakhine State, the Arakan Army has pushed to the edge of the state capital Sittwe; a junta amphibious landing on nearby Ngapyi Island in October was repulsed and several navy vessels were reported sunk. Fighting near Sittwe has displaced civilians from more than 70 villages, and more than 50,000 people have fled clashes around Kyaukphyu.

events.title: Junta landing on Ngapyi Island cleared
events.desc: Resistance monitors reported that junta troops who landed on Ngapyi Island near Sittwe on Oct 21–22 had been cleared out by the Arakan Army.

events.title: Arakan Army sinks navy vessels
events.desc: The Arakan Army reportedly sank two Tatmadaw warships near Sittwe, with some reports citing a third vessel destroyed. Claims are unverified.

events.title: Airstrike on Sittwe kills civilians
events.desc: A junta airstrike on Sittwe town reportedly killed 11 civilians, according to local sources.

events.title: 70 villages displaced near Sittwe
events.desc: Escalating clashes in Sittwe Township displaced civilians from more than 70 villages across three neighbouring townships.

events.title: Monitor warns of rising civilian killings
events.desc: ACLED reported more than a dozen mass killings in the first half of 2026, with over 450 civilian deaths, many in the central dry zone.

name: Sudan Civil War
status: Active Combat — Kordofan front, no truce
context: Sudan's war between the army (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces began in April 2023 and has produced the world's largest displacement crisis. After seizing El Fasher in October 2025, the RSF consolidated control over almost all of Darfur and shifted its offensive to Kordofan, besieging the army-held city of El Obeid. UN investigators say October 2026 recorded the highest number of drone attacks on civilians of the war, and accuse SAF security cells of mass arrests and torture in El Obeid. The US has proposed a 90-day humanitarian truce, but army chief al-Burhan rejects talks and vows to retake all territory. Less than half of the humanitarian appeal is funded, and malnutrition is rising in Darfur's camps.

events.title: Senior RSF commander defects
events.desc: A senior RSF commander announced his defection to the Sudanese Armed Forces.

events.title: UN: El Obeid civilians trapped
events.desc: The UN fact-finding mission said civilians in El Obeid are "trapped between drones and incarceration", with October the worst month for drone attacks on civilians since the war began.

events.title: US calls for humanitarian truce
events.desc: Washington pressed both sides to accept a humanitarian truce to allow aid deliveries. The RSF backs a truce but objects to parts of the withdrawal plan.

events.title: Aid appeal less than half funded
events.desc: Less than half of Sudan's humanitarian appeal had been funded as of 8 October; Kalma camp recorded 2,750 malnutrition cases in October.

events.title: Al-Burhan rejects talks
events.desc: Army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan rejected negotiations and vowed to retake all territory from the RSF, pointing to advances toward En Nahud and Al Khuway.

name: Sahel Insurgency
status: Escalating Insurgency — JNIM pressure on Bamako
context: The jihadist insurgency in the central Sahel, led by al-Qaeda affiliate JNIM and Islamic State Sahel, has spread across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, now ruled by military juntas aligned with Russia's Africa Corps. In April 2026 JNIM, allied with Tuareg separatists, launched a major offensive in Mali in which the defence minister was killed and the army pulled back from northern towns, although the army retook Kidal in early October. Since September JNIM has besieged Bamako and cut fuel supplies, and it is now attacking the capital's outskirts. In Burkina Faso, JNIM has staged a series of large assaults on army posts since February. Abuses by state forces and allied militias against civilians continue.

events.title: JNIM targets Bamako outskirts
events.desc: JNIM intensified attacks on army bases and the capital's outskirts, claiming 150 soldiers killed and 93 captured. Claims cannot be independently verified.

events.title: Malian army retakes Kidal
events.desc: The FLA retreated from Kidal in early October and the city returned to Malian army control.

events.title: Massacre in Kamona village
events.desc: Human Rights Watch reported that Malian soldiers and Dozo militiamen killed at least 21 men and burned homes in Kamona, Ségou region.

events.title: Escorted fuel convoys reach Bamako
events.desc: The junta pushed escorted convoys through the blockade, delivering more than a thousand fuel tankers since late October.

events.title: Siege of Bamako begins
events.desc: JNIM laid siege to Bamako and cut fuel supplies to the capital, according to HRW.

name: Taiwan Strait Tension
context: Beijing claims Taiwan as its territory and has steadily increased military pressure on the self-governed island. In December 2025 the PLA staged 'Justice Mission 2025', its largest drills around Taiwan to date, with over 130 aircraft sorties and coast guard participation. In October 2026 China answered President Lai Ching-te's National Day speech with live-fire artillery drills in five coastal zones far from Taiwan, while the PLA Navy made several large deployments into the Western Pacific through chokepoints north and south of the island, which analysts assess as rehearsals for blocking outside intervention. Taiwan's defence ministry is watching for a large-scale exercise in the November–December peak season.

events.title: PLA Navy deploys into Western Pacific
events.desc: AEI reported several large PLAN deployments through chokepoints around Taiwan since Oct 13, likely simulating a blockade against outside intervention.

events.title: US-Japan Keen Sword exercise begins
events.desc: US and Japanese forces began the Keen Sword exercise (Oct 19–29), which PLA naval movements appeared timed to shadow.

events.title: Taiwan braces for peak drill season
events.desc: Taiwan's defence ministry said it is monitoring for a large-scale PLA exercise as the November–December peak season approaches.

events.title: Live-fire drills after Lai speech
events.desc: China closed five coastal zones for artillery live-fire training. Taiwan said the zones were far from its waters, the closest 278 km away.

events.title: Lai delivers National Day speech
events.desc: President Lai Ching-te's National Day address drew punitive responses from Beijing rather than a named exercise.

name: Kashmir Conflict
context: India and Pakistan both claim the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, divided by the Line of Control since 1947–49. The region saw open fighting in May 2025 after the Pahalgam attack, ending in a ceasefire on 10 May 2025. Since then the situation has settled into persistent low-level tension: infiltration attempts, encounters with militants and cross-border firing along the LoC. Crisis Group rated the situation unchanged in October 2026. In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, protests over assembly seats left at least 40 dead in mid-2026.

events.title: Encounter with militants in Kupwara
events.desc: Indian security forces engaged militants in Kupwara district, according to conflict trackers.

events.title: Four killed in LoC landmine blast
events.desc: The Indian army said four alleged Pakistani militants died in a landmine explosion in Poonch near the LoC; Pakistani media described them as civilians.

events.title: Infiltration bid foiled in Rajouri
events.desc: The Indian Army said it thwarted an infiltration attempt in the Rajouri sector, with cross-border firing across the LoC.

events.title: Deadly unrest in Pakistani Kashmir
events.desc: At least 40 people, including 34 protesters and six security personnel, were killed in unrest over refugee seats in the local assembly.

name: Yemen Civil War
context: Yemen's war began when the Houthi movement seized Sanaa in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led intervention in 2015. Years of de facto truce have broken down: in recent weeks Saudi airstrikes have hit Houthi-held areas while the Houthis fire missiles and drones at southern Saudi Arabia. In September 2026 the Houthis seized the strategic Greater and Lesser Hanish islands in the southern Red Sea, tightening their grip on a key shipping lane. In early November strikes hit the Ras Isa oil terminal in Hodeidah and a telecom site near Saada; the Houthis claim more than 3,800 strikes since the escalation began. The war has killed an estimated 377,000 people, including indirect deaths, and left millions dependent on aid.

events.title: Strikes hit Ras Isa oil terminal
events.desc: Houthi media said "Saudi aggression" airstrikes hit the Ras Isa terminal in Hodeidah, damaging a berth and a commercial vessel, and a telecom site near Saada.

events.title: Saudi coalition intercepts missile
events.desc: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a drone and a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward southern Saudi Arabia.

events.title: Cross-border hostilities escalate
events.desc: Weeks of escalating exchanges saw Saudi strikes on Houthi areas and Houthi missile and drone launches into the kingdom.

events.title: Houthis seize Hanish islands
events.desc: The Houthis seized Greater and Lesser Hanish in the southern Red Sea, strengthening control over a key shipping route.

name: US/Israel–Iran War 2026
status: Active — no ceasefire; Strait of Hormuz crisis
context: The US and Israel went to war with Iran in late February 2026; the US campaign, Operation Epic Fury, was declared over on 5 May, but the conflict did not end. A Pakistan-brokered ceasefire in April was violated within hours, and a later Islamabad memorandum collapsed in July after Iran attacked commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz; it expired unextended in August. Fighting has killed thousands across Iran, Lebanon, Israel and the Gulf (early official counts: at least 1,300 in Iran, 880 in Lebanon), and the UN estimated up to 3.2 million displaced inside Iran. In early November the US struck Iranian air defences on Qeshm island after an apparent attack on a US aircraft. Qatari mediators have held talks, but Iran calls US proposals unconvincing.

events.title: Iran calls US reply "unconvincing"
events.desc: Tehran rejected Washington's response to its conditions for ending the war; no ceasefire is in force.

events.title: US strikes air defences on Qeshm
events.desc: US forces carried out limited "defensive" strikes on Iranian air-defence systems on Qeshm island after an apparent Iranian attack on a US aircraft.

events.title: Mariner killed in Hormuz attack
events.desc: A small Indian-crewed vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, killing at least one mariner.

events.title: Islamabad memorandum expires
events.desc: The June memorandum between Washington and Tehran expired without extension after collapsing in July.

events.title: Ceasefire collapses over Hormuz
events.desc: The US–Iran ceasefire broke down after Iran attacked commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

name: US Caribbean Drug War
status: Active — US strikes on alleged drug boats; post-Maduro Venezuela
context: Since September 2025 the US military has carried out lethal strikes on vessels it says were smuggling drugs in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, a campaign it frames as war against 'narco-terrorists'. The pressure culminated on 3 January 2026, when US special forces raided Caracas and captured Nicolás Maduro; Delcy Rodríguez has since served as acting leader. Boat strikes continued through 2026, reaching their 69th known strike in September, and the US has not presented public evidence that the vessels carried drugs. Death toll estimates vary between sources. The US is reportedly negotiating a status-of-forces agreement for troops in Venezuela and in June killed alleged Tren de Aragua leader Héctor 'Niño' Guerrero in an airstrike.

events.title: 69th boat strike kills four
events.desc: SOUTHCOM announced a strike on a go-fast vessel in the Caribbean that killed four people, the 69th such strike.

events.title: US troops deploy after earthquake
events.desc: Following a double earthquake, SOUTHCOM deployed about 2,000 troops to Venezuela and temporarily took control of the main airport.

events.title: Strike kills two in Caribbean
events.desc: A US strike on an alleged drug boat killed two people as the campaign ramped up again despite the Iran war.

events.title: US forces capture Maduro
events.desc: US special forces raided Caracas and flew Nicolás Maduro and his wife to New York; Delcy Rodríguez became acting leader.

name: US Somalia Counterterrorism Campaign
status: Active — al-Shabaab offensive, US & UAE strikes
context: Al-Shabaab, al-Qaeda's affiliate in Somalia, has fought the federal government and its foreign backers since 2007. The US conducts regular airstrikes against al-Shabaab and ISIS-Somalia in coordination with Mogadishu, including strikes on 17 and 19 October 2026. In late October al-Shabaab ambushed federal forces in South West State with car bombs and, reportedly, attack drones for the first time, and opened a new front in Puntland for the first time since early 2024. The UAE carried out its first reported strike in Somalia in almost a year. The AU's AUSSOM mission faces chronic funding shortfalls, the UN mission UNTMIS closed on 31 October, and the parliament speaker has accused politicians of colluding with the militants.

events.title: UN mission UNTMIS closes
events.desc: The UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia ended its mandate on 31 October.

events.title: UAE strike in Puntland
events.desc: The UAE reportedly struck militants planting roadside bombs in Puntland's Galgala pass, its first reported strike in Somalia since November 2025.

events.title: Al-Shabaab opens Puntland front
events.desc: IED and mortar attacks around Galgala, south of Bosaso, marked al-Shabaab's first operations against Puntland forces since early 2024.

events.title: AFRICOM strikes al-Shabaab
events.desc: US Africa Command conducted airstrikes on al-Shabaab on Oct 17 and 19 in coordination with the federal government.

events.title: Al-Shabaab ambush in South West State
events.desc: Al-Shabaab ambushed federal forces with car bombs and reportedly attack drones, a capability the group had not previously been confirmed to use.

name: DR Congo M23 War
context: The Rwanda-backed M23 rebellion re-emerged in eastern Congo in late 2021 and in early 2025 captured Goma and Bukavu, the capitals of North and South Kivu, which it still holds. A US-mediated deal between Kinshasa and Kigali and the Qatar-brokered Doha Framework, signed in November 2025, have not stopped the fighting; a ceasefire monitoring mechanism led by MONUSCO was mandated in February 2026, and an August roadmap tried to revive the delayed talks. The rebel coalition, now operating as the FRN, has threatened to quit the Doha process if Kinshasa goes ahead with a proposed constitutional referendum, while clashes with government forces intensify. Around 7 million people are displaced in Congo.

events.title: Rebels threaten to quit Doha talks
events.desc: The M23-led coalition said it would withdraw from the Doha Framework if Kinshasa holds a constitutional referendum, as fighting with government forces intensifies.

events.title: Peace roadmap agreed
events.desc: After talks in Switzerland, Kinshasa and AFC/M23 agreed a roadmap for the delayed Doha process and a standard method for reporting ceasefire violations.

events.title: Ceasefire monitoring mandate signed
events.desc: The parties signed a mandate for ceasefire monitoring teams led by MONUSCO with the ICGLR.

events.title: Doha Framework signed
events.desc: Kinshasa and AFC/M23 signed a framework for a comprehensive peace agreement in Qatar.

name: Syrian Conflict
status: Post-Assad transition — ISIS insurgency, Israeli operations
context: Fourteen years of civil war ended with the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024. President Ahmed al-Sharaa's transitional government now controls most of the country: a US-mediated 'Ceasefire and Full Integration Agreement' with the Kurdish-led SDF was announced in January 2026, the government took over ISIS detention sites and al-Hol camp, and former SDF fighters were absorbed into the army by August. ISIS declared a 'new phase of operations' against Damascus in February. In the south, Israel continues military activity around Quneitra; the US, Israel and Syria set up a joint communication cell, and talks on a southern security arrangement resumed around September, but no deal has been signed. Israel is wary of Syria rebuilding its air defences.

events.title: Israel warns of Syrian rearmament
events.desc: An Israeli defence official warned that al-Sharaa is rebuilding military capacity, including air defences, while courting international legitimacy.

events.title: Israel–Syria security talks resume
events.desc: Renewed contacts on a southern security arrangement were reported, alongside continued Israeli operations around Quneitra. No deal has been signed.

events.title: Former SDF fighters join army
events.desc: Former SDF units were absorbed into the Syrian army, completing government takeover of the northeast.

events.title: ISIS declares "new phase"
events.desc: ISIS announced a new phase of operations against the al-Sharaa government and killed security personnel.

events.title: Damascus–SDF integration deal
events.desc: A US-mediated ceasefire and full integration agreement between al-Sharaa and SDF commander Mazloum Abdi was announced.

name: Haiti Gang Crisis
status: Active — gangs control most of Port-au-Prince
context: Haiti has been engulfed by gang violence since the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse in 2021. The Viv Ansanm coalition led by Jimmy 'Barbecue' Chérizier, designated a terrorist organisation by the US in 2025, controls an estimated 70–90% of Port-au-Prince and has expanded into the Artibonite and Centre departments. The UN Security Council replaced the Kenya-led mission with a Gang Suppression Force in September 2025 and extended it on 29 September 2026, but only about 1,000 of an authorised 5,500 personnel are deployed. In August 2026 a gang attack on a farming community in Kenscoff killed 30 people. Elections have repeatedly slipped amid the insecurity.

events.title: Airlift for Gang Suppression Force
events.desc: A large airlift of equipment for the Gang Suppression Force was reported as the mission works toward full capacity.

events.title: UN extends Gang Suppression Force
events.desc: The Security Council renewed the GSF mandate; only about 1,000 of 5,500 authorised personnel are on the ground.

events.title: Kenscoff attack kills 30
events.desc: A gang attack on a farming community in Kenscoff, south of Port-au-Prince, killed 30 people; officials blamed Viv Ansanm.

events.title: Clashes inside Viv Ansanm
events.desc: ACLED reported infighting within the coalition but judged a collapse of the alliance unlikely.

name: Mexican Drug War
status: Active — Sinaloa civil war, CJNG after El Mencho
context: Mexico's war against drug cartels, launched in 2006, has killed hundreds of thousands. The Sinaloa Cartel has been split by a civil war between the Chapitos and Mayos factions for more than two years since the arrest of 'El Mayo' Zambada, with violence shifting from Culiacán to southern Sinaloa and Mazatlán. In February 2026 Mexican special forces, acting on CIA intelligence, killed CJNG leader Nemesio 'El Mencho' Oseguera, raising fears of a similar fragmentation. President Sheinbaum has pledged to keep troops in Sinaloa and blames US actions for fuelling the violence, while cooperation with US intelligence, including expanded CIA surveillance flights, has deepened.

events.title: Intimidation banner in Mazatlán
events.desc: A banner exposing three women appeared in Mazatlán, part of continued intimidation amid the factional war.

events.title: Decapitated body found in Culiacán
events.desc: A decapitated man was found behind Plaza San Isidro with a note blaming rival cartel members.

events.title: Mazatlán prison riot kills 10
events.desc: A fight at El Castillo prison left 10 dead and 16 injured; authorities did not say if it was linked to the cartel war.

events.title: Sheinbaum keeps troops in Sinaloa
events.desc: Visiting Sinaloa, President Sheinbaum promised no Navy, Army or National Guard troops would be withdrawn as fighting shifted to Mazatlán.

events.title: CJNG leader El Mencho killed
events.desc: Mexican special forces, acting on CIA intelligence, killed CJNG leader Nemesio Oseguera.

name: Northern Ethiopia War (Tigray)
context: The 2020–2022 Tigray war, one of the deadliest conflicts of the century, ended with the Pretoria agreement, but the deal unravelled. On 23 September 2026 large-scale hostilities broke out when TPLF and Amhara Fano forces attacked federal positions, with the heaviest fighting in North Wollo. Federal forces captured the Tigray capital Mekelle and advanced north and west; Reuters, AFP and ACLED report Eritrean troops crossing into Tigray, which Asmara denies. Fano has joined the TPLF and five other regional rebel groups in an alliance to overthrow the federal government, and Ethiopia and Eritrea are on the brink of direct conflict. On 3 November the TPLF claimed a counter-attack killed some 500 government soldiers and militiamen.

events.title: TPLF claims major counter-attack
events.desc: The TPLF said its counter-attack killed about 500 and wounded 800 government soldiers and allied militiamen. Addis Ababa gave no account.

events.title: TPLF sidelines interim administration
events.desc: The TPLF moved to consolidate control of Tigray, pushing aside the federally backed interim administration.

events.title: Federal forces capture Mekelle
events.desc: Ethiopian federal forces took the Tigray capital and advanced toward strategic towns; Eritrean troops reportedly crossed into Tigray.

events.title: Large-scale war erupts
events.desc: TPLF and Fano forces attacked federal and allied positions, with the heaviest fighting in North Wollo.

name: India–Pakistan Conflict 2025
context: After militants killed 26 people at Pahalgam in Indian-administered Kashmir on 22 April 2025, India launched Operation Sindoor against targets in Pakistan in May, triggering the most serious military exchange between the nuclear-armed neighbours in decades, including missile, drone and artillery strikes. A ceasefire took effect on 10 May 2025 and has broadly held. Relations remain frozen, and tension persists along the Line of Control through infiltration attempts, landmine incidents and encounters with militants, which Crisis Group rated as unchanged in October 2026.

events.title: LoC landmine blast kills four
events.desc: India said four Pakistani militants died in a landmine explosion in Poonch; Pakistan said they were civilians.

events.title: CrisisWatch: situation unchanged
events.desc: Crisis Group rated India–Pakistan tensions unchanged in October 2026, citing disputes over border killings.

events.title: Ceasefire announced
events.desc: India and Pakistan agreed to halt military action after four days of cross-border strikes.

events.title: India launches Operation Sindoor
events.desc: India struck targets in Pakistan and Pakistani-administered Kashmir; Pakistan retaliated with artillery, drones and missiles.

events.title: Pahalgam attack
events.desc: Militants killed 26 people, mostly tourists, near Pahalgam in Indian-administered Kashmir.
